column1: # Tool-usage rules. One per line, tab-separated:
#   id <TAB> ERE matched against the Bash command <TAB> message <TAB> incident
# THE BAR: a rule belongs here only if the idiom fails SILENTLY — it hands back
# a confident wrong answer rather than an error. Anything that errors out is
# already self-announcing and must not be added; a rule that fires on healthy
# commands trains dismissal and is worse than no rule at all.
# Never append blindly: a lesson that is a special case of a rule here EXTENDS
# that rule rather than growing a sibling. Fusion is the whole anti-bloat
# discipline. A pattern is inadmissible until it is shown to catch the bad
# command AND leave a healthy one alone.

column3: The exit status (`$?`, and the one Bash reports) is the LAST command's: a test or build piped into head/tail, or followed by `; echo` / `; tail log`, reads as exit 0 when it failed. Redirect to a log and grep the verdict line, or put the real command last.
column4: 2026-08 a test run with 102 failing files piped into `tail -25` returned 0 and was reported as passing; `| head -3; echo "exit=$?"` printed exit=0 for a symbol that exists nowhere.

column3: `/tmp` is shared by every concurrent session and worktree: another run can overwrite or interleave this file, and it still ends on a plausible success line. Write it to the session scratchpad.
column4: A generic `/tmp` test log was overwritten by a session in another worktree and still ended in "All tests passed!".

column3: No UTF-8 locale on this machine: `wc -m` and `cut -c` count BYTES. CJK is miscounted and truncation splits characters mid-sequence.
column4: 2026-08-21 `cut -c1-120` split multi-byte characters in CJK report lines; ugrep also aborted on a CJK pattern.

column3: `dart format` on a directory, or `dart fix --apply` without `--code=<rule> <paths>`, rewrites untouched siblings and buries the real change in the diff. Pass only the files this turn edited.
column4: Learned in two repos before either wrote it down; one `dart format lib/` put 13 unrelated files in the diff.

column3: BSD sed (macOS) has no `\b`: the substitution matches nothing and still exits 0. Use `[[:<:]]` / `[[:>:]]`, a plain pattern, or `perl -pi -e`.

This resets the file to HEAD, not to "before my edit": uncommitted work already in it is lost, with no stash or blob to recover. If `git status --porcelain <file>` was not clean before your change, reverse the exact edit or restore a `cp` backup instead.
column4: 2026-08 and 2026-09, in two repos: undoing a deliberate test-break with `git checkout --` wiped an uncommitted refactor in the same file.

column3: This counts OCCURRENCES, not distinct values — pipe through `sort -u` first if the number is going to be reported as "how many different things".
column4: raw occurrence count reported as a distinct count

column3: A path beginning with '-' (every ~/.claude/projects/ folder does) is parsed as a FLAG by grep/ls/stat/cat; with stderr silenced it returns 0 matches and reads as 'nothing found'. Prefix ./ or put -- before it.
column4: Path starting with '-' is parsed as a flag by grep/ls/stat; with stderr silenced it reads as 'nothing found'

column3: Python pollutes the system, and the install succeeds — no error tells you this was the wrong road. First look for a native tool already on the machine (hb-subset / bash / iconv / bsdtar / curl / a single-file node script). Propose Python only when no non-Python route exists, and then in an isolated venv, said out loud. Exempt: a one-off `python3 -c` that installs nothing.
column4: Founder: "I really dislike how Python pollutes the system" — a finished fontTools font build was thrown out whole and replaced with tool/fonts/build_fonts.sh
